name: Question 16
worked_solution:
From the identity  $1+{tan}^{2}⁡\theta ={sec}^{2}⁡\theta $ with $\theta =(5x+\pi ),$ we get 

$$
1+{tan}^{2}⁡(5x+\pi )={sec}^{2}⁡(5x+\pi ).
$$

Substituting the above into our integral gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (9{tan}^{2}⁡(5x+\pi )-5{x}^{4}+9)\,\text{d}x & =\int (9[1+{tan}^{2}⁡(5x+\pi )]-5{x}^{4})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int (9{sec}^{2}⁡(5x+\pi )-5{x}^{4})\,\text{d}x \\  & =9\cdot (\frac{1}{5}\operatorname{tan}⁡(5x+\pi ))-5\cdot \frac{{x}^{5}}{5}+C \\  & =\frac{9}{5}\operatorname{tan}⁡(5x+\pi )-{x}^{5}+C.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 16
?

Calculate ∫(9tan2⁡(5x+π)−5x4+9)dx.

a
95tan⁡(5x+π)+x55+C
b
95tan⁡(5x+π)−x5+C
c
95tan⁡(5x+π)−x55+C
d
52tan⁡(5x+π)−x5+C
e
92tan⁡(5x+π)−x5+C
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

From the identity 1+tan2⁡θ=sec2⁡θ with θ=(5x+π), we get

1+tan2⁡(5x+π)=sec2⁡(5x+π).

Substituting the above into our integral gives ∫(9tan2⁡(5x+π)−5x4+9)dx=∫(9[1+tan2⁡(5x+π)]−5x4)dx=∫(9sec2⁡(5x+π)−5x4)dx=9⋅(15tan⁡(5x+π))−5⋅x55+C=95tan⁡(5x+π)−x5+C.
